rot.edge.ideia.ex1.e1: Now from Black's side. The pawns are locked, each with another in front of it, and only the kings move: whoever must move without a good king move is in zugzwang.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.e4: The white king's target is the pawn on c5: if your king moves away, it falls. To defend it, your king always goes to the white king's rank and leaves an odd number of squares between them.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.livre.fala: Keep playing as Black and see how White attacks.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.p: Black to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.certo: On a7, your king stands on the same rank as the white king, with three squares between them.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to take the king to a7, on the same rank as the white king, with three squares between them.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6a6.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6a6.2: The white king goes to e6, on the same rank. There are three squares between the kings, counting the pawn on c6, and Black is to move: White has the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6c7.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6c7.2: The white king goes to e6. If the black king returns to b6, the white king reaches d6 and keeps the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6a5.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6a5.2: The white king goes to d7. If the black king returns to b6, the white king reaches d6 and keeps the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6b7.1: After this move, White can win.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.err.b6b7.2: The white king goes to d7, on the same rank. Only c7 lies between the kings and Black is to move: White has the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.1: Three squares between the kings, and White is to move: an odd number, so you have the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.2: The white king approaches along the seventh rank, towards the black pawns.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.3: You answer on b7. Only c7 lies between the kings: you still have the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.4: The white king steps down to d6 and attacks the pawn on c5.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.5: You defend with the king on b6. The pawn on c6 stands between the kings, and it counts as a square: just one, an odd number.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.6: The opposition is yours: your king defends both pawns, and the white king, with no pawn move to spend, is in zugzwang and must retreat.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.8: And if your king goes to c7? Only d7 lies between the kings, which also looks like an odd opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.8b: The white king goes to e6. Now the odd square would be a6, and from c7 your king cannot reach it: White gets the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex1.l.9: That is why a7 is the right square: if the white king changes rank, your king follows him and leaves an odd number of squares.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.e2: Now with White, against the same locked pawns: your king wants to capture the ones on c5 and c6. The kings are on the same rank, with three squares between them, and White to move: the opposition is Black's.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.e5: If your king approaches, the black king follows and keeps the odd number. But look: the pawn on c4 guards b5, and the one on a3 guards b4, and the black king cannot go to those squares.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.livre.fala: Keep playing as White and see how Black defends.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.p: White to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.certo: With the king on f5, the black king cannot keep the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to move the king away to f5. It looks strange, but this way the opposition becomes yours.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5d6.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5d6.2: The black king goes to b6. Only the pawn on c6 lies between the kings and White is to move: Black has the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5f6.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5f6.2: The black king goes to b6, on the same rank. There are three squares between the kings and White is to move: Black has the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5e6.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5e6.2: The black king goes to a6, on the same rank. There are three squares between the kings and White is to move: Black has the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5e4.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5e4.2: The black king climbs to a6. With your king on the fourth rank, when it reaches the sixth the black king answers on the same rank with an odd number.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5f4.1: After this move, White no longer wins: Black can draw.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.err.e5f4.2: The black king climbs to b6. With your king on the fourth rank, when it reaches the sixth the black king answers on the same rank with an odd number.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.2: Four squares between the kings, and Black to move. To get back to an odd number, the black king would have to go to b5, but the pawn on c4 guards that square.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.4: So the black king leaves the fifth rank and goes up to b6, near its pawns.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.5: You climb with him, to f6. Three squares between the kings: you have the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.6: With no pawn move available, the black king has to move. He climbs to b7, hoping for a rank where you cannot follow him.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.7: You climb again, to f7. Three squares between the kings: it is the distant opposition, and it is still yours.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.13: Back to the start. The key was the first move: with the king on f5, an even number, the black king could not get back to odd, because the square it needed was guarded by a pawn.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.curiosidades: This position appears in the chapter "Practical Endgame using opposition", from a study on the distant opposition published on Lichess by Brandon2021. The link opens the study.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.7b: The black king goes to a7. Four squares are left between the kings, an even number, and now White is to move.
rot.edge.demos.longe.1: Attack demonstration. Five squares between the kings, the pawn included, and White is to move: Black has the opposition.
rot.edge.demos.longe.2: The white king retreats: four squares, and Black to move. Odd would require b5, but the pawn on c4 guards that square.
rot.edge.demos.longe.4: So the black king must leave the fifth rank and climbs to a6.
rot.edge.demos.longe.5: The white king follows: three squares, White's opposition. The retreat decided it.
rot.edge.demos.escolha.1: Attack demonstration. Two squares leave an odd number between the kings: e6 and g6. Which is right?
rot.edge.demos.escolha.2: With the king on e6, only d6 is left: an odd number. But the white king moves away from the h5 pawn, and the win is already gone.
rot.edge.demos.escolha.3: The black king counterattacks: it runs to c4, toward the a3 pawn, and the white king follows it.
rot.edge.demos.escolha.4: The white king goes to e4 and to d3, but arrives too late: the black king is already on b3, beside the a3 pawn.
rot.edge.demos.escolha.5: The black king captures the a3 pawn: now the white king only draws by going to c2 or c3.
rot.edge.demos.escolha.6: Let us go back to the starting position and choose the other square, the one closer to the h5 pawn.
rot.edge.demos.escolha.7: With the king on g6, three squares remain: also odd. And the white king attacks the h5 pawn.
rot.edge.demos.escolha.8: The black king runs to the h4 pawn via d7 and e7, but the white king captures the h5 pawn first.
rot.edge.demos.escolha.9: The white king returns to g6, and the h4 pawn runs free: White wins.
rot.edge.demos.oitava.1: Attacking demonstration: the pawn on e6 guards d7 and f7, and the black king can only leave the eighth rank via c7. Taking away c7, the white king traps the black king and enters the seventh towards the pawn on e7.
rot.edge.demos.oitava.3: On b6, the white king takes away c7 and takes the diagonal opposition. On c6, it would give up the opposition: the black king would go to c8.
rot.edge.demos.oitava.5: The black king goes to c8: c7 is next to the white king, and the eighth is its only rank.
rot.edge.demos.oitava.6: The white king takes the direct opposition on c6, and the black king, forced to move, has to step aside.
rot.edge.demos.oitava.7: The black king goes to d8, to guard c7, but the white king enters the seventh rank via b7.
rot.edge.demos.oitava.8: The black king only has e8, and the white king goes on to c7, taking d8 away.
rot.edge.demos.oitava.9: The black king only has f8: d8 is next to the white king, and the e6 pawn guards d7 and f7.
rot.edge.demos.oitava.10: The white king reaches d7 and attacks the e7 pawn. The black king defends it from f8, but it is his move: he can only go to g7 or g8.
rot.edge.demos.oitava.11: The white king captures the pawn on e7, and White wins: the pawns guarded the king's exits, and the opposition took away the last one.
rot.edge.demos.contagem.1: Defensive demonstration, and Black to move. Between the kings, d6 and the pawn on c6: even. Your king must leave an odd number.
rot.edge.demos.contagem.3: Your king goes to a6. Now b6, c6 and d6 are between them: three squares, and White is to move. The opposition is yours.
rot.edge.demos.contagem.4: The white king goes to d6 and threatens the pawn on c5.
rot.edge.demos.contagem.5: Your king returns to b6 and defends both pawns: only c6 between the kings, and White is to move, in zugzwang.
rot.edge.demos.contagem.ponte: Your turn against the machine: first an attack, with White, then a defence, with Black. Count the squares between the kings, pawns included.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.7c: Your king goes to e7: three squares, and the opposition is still yours. g7 would also win, but between two squares that leave an odd number, take the one closer to the black pawns.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.7d: The black king goes back to b7 to defend the c6 pawn. c7 and d7 are left: two squares, an even number.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.7e: Your king goes to d7. Only c7 is left between the kings: an odd number, and the opposition is still yours.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.7f: The black king has to move and goes to a7. On b6, your king would go to d6 and keep the opposition.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.7g: Your king captures the c6 pawn, which was left undefended.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.7h: The black king goes to a6, but cannot reach the c5 pawn: the c4 pawn guards b5.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.7i: Your king also captures the c5 pawn, and White wins: this is what the opposition was preparing.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.enunciado: Play White: capture the d7 pawn.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.fim: The d7 pawn is captured. The detour via g6 gave Black the move with the kings face to face on the f-file, and the black king stayed trapped on the eighth rank.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.cedo.1: On f6, your king arrives too early: the black king goes to the f-file, in front of it, and the win slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.cedo.2: The black king goes to f8, on the same file. Only f7 is left between the kings, and White is to move: the opposition is Black's.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.porta.1: This move leaves f7 free, the only square through which the black king leaves the eighth rank, and the win slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.porta.2: The black king leaves the eighth rank via f7, the only exit: off that rank, it is no longer trapped.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.desce.1: This move takes your king away from the black king, and the win slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.desce.2: With your king far away, the black king leaves the eighth rank via f7, and White no longer wins.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.solta.1: This move lets the black king leave the eighth rank: now it is Black who wins.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.solta.2: The black king leaves the eighth rank and heads for the d6 pawn: your king, too far away, cannot defend it in time.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.enunciado: Play Black: when the white king changes rank, answer on the same rank and leave an odd number of squares between the kings.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.fim: Your king answered on the white king's rank every move, always with one square between them, and the e6 and e5 pawns stayed protected.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.par.1: That move leaves two squares between the kings, an even number, and your king no longer protects the e6 pawn: the draw slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.par.2: The white king captures the e6 pawn and then the e5 pawn: the e4 pawn advances with the king beside it and promotes.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.fora.1: That move does not bring your king to the white king's rank and leaves the e6 pawn undefended: the draw slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.fora.2: The white king captures the e6 pawn and then the e5 pawn. If your king returns to the e4 pawn, the white king goes to the a6 pawn, and the a5 pawn promotes.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.corre.1: On c5, your king runs to the a5 pawn and abandons the e6 and e5 pawns: the white king captures both, and the draw slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.corre.2: The white king captures the e6 pawn and then the e5 pawn. Even if your king captures the a5 pawn, the e4 pawn promotes first.
rot.edge.ideia.ex2.l.16: Next, the same resource in other positions, up to a king trapped on the eighth rank: the pawns guard its exits, and the opposition takes away the last one.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.soltag7.1: This move lets the black king leave the eighth rank: now it is Black who wins.
rot.edge.pratica.ataque.err.soltag7.2: The black king leaves the eighth rank via g7 and takes the opposition: it reaches the d6 pawn, and your king cannot defend it.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.parc7.1: That move leaves two squares between the kings, an even number, and your king no longer protects the e6 pawn: the draw slips away.
rot.edge.pratica.defesa.err.parc7.2: The white king captures the e6 pawn and then the e5 pawn. If your king returns to the e4 pawn, the white king goes to the a6 pawn, and the a5 pawn promotes.
